# Yaps plugins for Codex

> Five focused Codex plugins use one Yaps desktop installation for persistent local Markdown memory, live dictation, media transcription, SRT subtitle generation, and text-to-speech.

## Canonical facts

- Marketplace: Yaps
- Repository: https://github.com/richawo/yaps-codex-plugin
- Website: https://www.yaps.ai/
- Download: https://yaps.ai/download
- Publisher: Yaps AI
- License for plugin packages: MIT
- Category: Productivity
- Yaps desktop platforms: macOS and Windows
- Shared dependency: the separately installed Yaps desktop application
- Authentication: handled only inside Yaps; plugins never receive credentials or tokens
- Local integration: Yaps ships `yaps_mcp` for memory and `yaps_cli` for local automation

## Plugins

- Yaps Memory: persistent cross-chat memory, remembered facts, personal knowledge, local Markdown search, citations, and permission-controlled updates.
- Yaps Dictation: system-wide voice typing setup, readiness checks, troubleshooting, and recent-dictation recovery.
- Yaps Transcription: existing audio or video to a plain-text transcript.
- Yaps SRT Generator: existing audio or video to a timestamped `.srt` subtitle file.
- Yaps Text to Speech: text or text files to local WAV or PCM speech.

## Important boundaries

- Installing a plugin does not create, host, or upload a vault.
- Yaps Memory is not native ChatGPT/model memory and does not modify model weights.
- Yaps Dictation does not intercept Codex's built-in microphone button; Yaps uses its own configurable global shortcut.
- File transcription and SRT generation use the installed Yaps engine and do not silently switch to a hosted provider.
- Text-to-speech preserves the supplied script unless rewriting was explicitly requested.
- The repository contains no user data, credentials, telemetry client, private Yaps application source, or speech-model binaries.

## Installation

1. Download Yaps desktop: https://yaps.ai/download
2. Add the marketplace: `codex plugin marketplace add richawo/yaps-codex-plugin`
3. Install the desired `yaps-*@yaps` plugins.
4. In Yaps, use Connect Codex for Memory and Install CLI for file/speech automation.
5. Start a new Codex task.
